title: Abusing Active Directory Certificate Services: ESC13 and Beyond in Hybrid Forests
description: SpecterOps researchers demonstrate new attack primitives exploiting misconfigured enterprise certificate enrollment policies and OID group mapping to achieve stealthy domain escalation in hybrid Active Directory environments.
content:
Active Directory Certificate Services (ADCS) continues to be an adversary favorite for achieving silent domain-wide compromise. In this research, we unpack ESC13, an enrollment vector stemming from subtle inconsistencies in how issuance policies map to domain authorization groups.

When an enrollment template enforces custom application policies, operators often assume membership in the target policy provides segregation. We demonstrate that misaligned OID definitions permit an unprivileged workstation account to enroll a certificate that Microsoft Entra ID and Kerberos Key Distribution Centers (KDCs) treat as fully privileged Domain Admin credentials.
author: SpecterOps Research Team

title: Evasive Payload Delivery: Crafting In-Memory Shellcode Loaders with Indirect Syscalls
description: Deep dive into modern evasion techniques using indirect system calls, synthetic stack frame construction, and hardware breakpoint instrumentation to bypass contemporary EDR memory scanners.
content:
Endpoint Detection and Response (EDR) sensors rely heavily on API hooking in ntdll.dll to inspect telemetry before execution passes to the kernel. In this technical walkthrough, OffSec instructors break down the engineering of an indirect syscall loader.

By bouncing execution through legitimate syscall; ret stubs inside ntdll rather than issuing raw syscall instructions, offensive operators can preserve call-stack telemetry and evade return address heuristics.
author: OffSec Research

title: Exploiting AWS IAM Role Trust Policies for Stealthy Multi-Account Lateral Movement
description: Praetorian offensive engineers detail how subtle wildcards in AWS IAM AssumeRole trust policies enable cross-account pivoting and control-plane persistence without generating CloudTrail anomalous IP alerts.
content: Complex cloud organizations often have thousands of cross-account IAM trust relationships. In this research, we review automated discovery tooling to map role-chaining pathways that allow red team operators to navigate from an untrusted staging VPC all the way to sensitive production accounts.
author: Praetorian Cloud Offensive Practice

title: From Fake Installer to Domain Admin: Analyzing an 8-Hour LockBit Intrusion
description: A comprehensive forensic reconstruction of a fast-moving ransomware intrusion that began with SEO-poisoned software installers, transitioned through Cobalt Strike beacons, and achieved full domain encryption in less than 8 hours.
content: In this in-depth case study, we document the forensic artifacts left behind during an end-to-end LockBit affiliate intrusion. The initial vector was a weaponized utility downloaded via malvertising. Within 45 minutes of execution, the threat actor established a C2 channel, harvested LSASS credentials, and utilized Remote Desktop Protocol (RDP) to pivot across backup servers.
author: The DFIR Report

title: Hunting Illicit App Registrations and OAuth Consent Abuse in Microsoft 365
description: Practical detection engineering strategies for identifying malicious OAuth consent grants, rogue Entra ID applications, and high-privilege Microsoft Graph API tokens used by persistent adversaries.
content: Adversaries are increasingly shifting from credential stuffing to OAuth application consent grants. Once a user clicks Accept on a crafted consent prompt, the attacker receives a persistent OAuth refresh token that bypasses MFA and password resets entirely.
author: Huntress Threat Research

title: The Race to Red-Team Frontier AI Models: What Independent Testers Actually Found
description: Independent evaluation consortiums publish comprehensive security audits of the latest reasoning models, revealing stubborn prompt injection vulnerabilities and unintended cyber-offensive tradecraft disclosures.
content: As autonomous AI agents are given shell access and API keys to manage production software, security evaluators are testing the limits of alignment guardrails. The latest report highlights that while basic jailbreaks are quickly filtered, multi-turn cognitive priming techniques still permit unauthorized capability discovery.
author: The Verge Tech Policy Desk

title: Enterprise Hybrid Cloud Architecture: Real-World Zero Trust Implementation
description: How enterprise CIOs and CISOs are navigating microsegmentation, continuous identity verification, and multi-cloud perimeter security without crushing developer velocity.
content: Zero Trust has matured from a marketing buzzword into rigorous architectural mandate. This guide evaluates modern identity-aware proxies, mutual TLS enforcement, and dynamic access policies across AWS, Azure, and legacy data centers.
author: ZDNET Enterprise Strategy

title: Hardware Security Keys: The Essential Buyer’s Guide to FIDO2 and WebAuthn
description: From USB-C and NFC keys to biometric tokens, we test the fastest, most durable hardware authentication keys that make credential theft and phishing mathematically impossible.
content: Physical security keys represent the single most effective defense against modern phishing kits and session token hijackers. We put the top models through rigorous real-world durability and compatibility testing across iOS, macOS, Windows, and Linux.
author: Engadget Hardware Review

title: Inside Android’s Kernel Evolution: How Rust and Hardware Tagging Squelched Memory Corruption
description: A deep dive into ARM Memory Tagging Extension (MTE) and Rust driver architecture in modern Android kernels, and how they make zero-day privilege escalation exponentially more difficult.
content: Memory safety vulnerabilities have historically accounted for the vast majority of severe Android kernel exploits. By pairing hardware-enforced memory tagging with first-class Rust development for new HALs and drivers, Google and silicon partners are reshaping mobile security architectures.
author: XDA Mobile Engineering Team

title: Passkeys Explained: How to Finally Ditch Passwords in 2026
description: A clear, step-by-step tutorial on setting up passkeys across Apple Keychain, Google Password Manager, and 1Password, plus how to secure account recovery if your devices are lost.
content: Passkeys have rapidly expanded from early adoption to mainstream support across Google, Apple, Microsoft, Amazon, and leading banking apps. Here is everything you need to know about setting them up, backing them up securely, and understanding the cryptographic private-key pairs running under the hood.
author: How-To Geek Editorial

title: The Essential Digital Hygiene Checklist: Lock Down Your Accounts in 30 Minutes
description: A high-impact checklist to audit active device logins, revoke stale OAuth permissions, prune third-party data brokers, and harden your personal threat surface.
content: Most personal cyber compromises don’t come from cinematic zero-days—they happen because an old connected app retained permission to your email for six years. Use this weekend checklist to audit your digital footprint and restore tight control over your personal data.
author: Lifehacker Tech Tips

title: macOS Sequoia Security Deep Dive: Local Network Prompts, Gatekeeper, and Keychain Sync
description: An examination of Apple’s updated security architecture in macOS Sequoia, covering the new local network device access dialogs, revamped Gatekeeper notarization requirements, and Apple Passwords standalone app.
content: With macOS Sequoia, Apple continues tightening security boundaries on the Mac desktop. Apps must now request explicit user permission before probing your local Wi-Fi network, and unsigned binaries can no longer be easily bypassed via Control-click without visiting System Settings.
author: MacRumors Analysis

title: Android 15 Private Space: How Google’s New OS Sandboxing Protects Confidential Apps
description: How Android 15 creates a completely isolated Android profile with separate credential encryption keys, preventing background telemetry and snooping when your phone is shared or confiscated.
content: Android 15 introduces Private Space, an isolated sandbox that keeps sensitive banking, crypto, and messaging applications hidden behind biometric barriers. When locked, apps inside Private Space are stopped completely—stopping background location access, notifications, and memory residency.
author: 9to5Google Mobile Team

title: Global Website Blocking Orders Trigger Major Battle Over Encrypted DNS Privacy Standards
description: Court orders in Europe and Latin America demanding that public DNS resolvers like Cloudflare and Quad9 implement domain blocking spark pushback from internet freedom advocates over encrypted DNS integrity.
content: The push by media copyright holders to force public recursive DNS resolvers into serving filtered answers is coming to a critical legal head. Rights groups warn that forcing DNS-over-HTTPS (DoH) providers to tamper with cryptographic resolution sets a dangerous precedent for global state censorship.
author: TorrentFreak Legal Desk

title: Is This A Joke? In The Auth Header? F5 BIG-IP UnAuth Heap-Overflow to RCE (CVE-2026-94127)
description: watchTowr Labs analyzes a critical unauthenticated remote code execution vulnerability in F5 BIG-IP appliances stemming from a heap overflow in the TMUI HTTP Authorization header processing routine.
content: F5 BIG-IP appliances sit at the core of enterprise network perimeters. In our latest advisory, we demonstrate how malformed base64 credentials in the HTTP Basic Auth header trigger an out-of-bounds heap write in TMOS, allowing remote unauthenticated attackers to execute arbitrary system code with root privileges.
author: Sina Kheirkhah (@SinSinology)

title: Considerations for Critical Infrastructure Operators Working With Third-Party ICS Integrators
description: The Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) and CISA publish joint guidance urging critical infrastructure operators to enforce principle of least privilege (PoLP) and strict supply chain verification for third-party industrial control systems (ICS) and SCADA vendors.
content: The Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) and Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) have released joint guidance to highlight considerations for critical infrastructure entities to reduce risk and minimize vulnerabilities when working with third-party industrial control system (ICS) integrators.
author: CISA / FBI

title: Corp MDM Spyware Targets Logistics Firms, Steals SMS and Redirects Calls
description: The logistics sector has become the target of a new malicious cyber campaign that distributes an Android spyware codenamed Corp MDM disguised as enterprise device management services.
content: The logistics sector has become the target of a new malicious cyber campaign that distributes an Android spyware codenamed Corp MDM. The malware requests broad permissions allowing it to read SMS messages, forward two-factor authentication tokens, and reroute operational calls.
author: The Hacker News

title: Dissecting Lumma Stealer v4: Anti-Analysis Tricks, Process Hollowing, and C2 Infrastructure
description: ANY.RUN malware analysts dissect the latest Lumma Stealer variant, uncovering novel control flow flattening, sandbox evasion heuristics, and automated browser credential extraction.
content: Lumma Stealer remains one of the most prolific information stealers in the cybercrime underground. In this interactive sandbox breakdown, we trace how Lumma unpacks itself in memory, injects into legitimate Windows processes, and rapidly harvests crypto wallets and session cookies.
author: ANY.RUN Malware Research

title: Peer Pressure: Inside the Multi-National Sality Botnet Disruption Operation
description: CrowdStrike Counter Adversary Operations details the technical takedown of the resilient peer-to-peer Sality botnet infrastructure conducted in collaboration with global law enforcement.
content: Sality has plagued enterprise endpoints for over a decade. By poisoning the botnet’s decentralized peer-to-peer routing tables and sinkholing key command relays, our threat hunting team neutralized thousands of infected nodes globally.
author: CrowdStrike Counter Adversary Operations

title: Dark Web Bulletin: Ransomware Gangs Log 184 New Extortion Victims in 72 Hours
description: Telemetry from dark web leak sites reveals a sharp surge in ransomware extortion claims targeting manufacturing, healthcare, and state education sectors.
content: Monitoring across 42 active ransomware extortion blogs reveals an unprecedented spike in double-extortion listings. Attackers are leaking sensitive employee records and internal communications following unheeded ransom deadlines.
author: Daily Dark Web Intelligence Desk
